passages.text: I, Clement, a citizen of Rome, have managed to live the first part of my life with self-control, while from childhood my reflection kept turning the desire within me toward states of dejection and pain. For a thought about death stayed with me—I do not know where it began—repeatedly reminding me that, once dead, I would not exist and no one would ever make mention of me, since boundless time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion: I will be nonexistent, not knowing those who exist, not knowing, not being known, not having come into being, and not coming into being. And did the world ever come into being, and what, then, existed before it came into being? For if it always existed, it also will exist; but if it came into being, it will also be dissolved. And after its dissolution, what in turn will exist, unless perhaps silence and oblivion? And perhaps there will be something that cannot now be conceived.

source_issues.source_quote: ἔσομαι δὲ οὐκ ὤν, οὐκ ὄντας εἰδώς
source_issues.issue: The verified wording is syntactically defensible but permits two scopes for οὐκ in the second phrase: “not knowing those who exist” or “knowing those who do not exist.” The contextual rendering is given in the text without emending the Greek.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to live ... with self-control
lexical_decisions.rationale: σωφρόνως can denote chastity more narrowly, but here broadly describes a restrained early life.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς ἐννοίας μου ἐκ παιδὸς ἀπασχολούσης τὴν ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐπιθυμίαν εἴς τε ἀθυμίας καὶ πόνους
lexical_decisions.chosen: while from childhood my reflection kept turning the desire within me toward states of dejection and pain
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive absolute describes his reflection as occupying or diverting his inward desire toward distress.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ ἀπείρου χρόνου πάντων τὰ πάντα εἰς λήθην φέροντος
lexical_decisions.chosen: since boundless time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the universal πάντων and the comprehensive τὰ πάντα.

lexical_decisions.chosen: not knowing those who exist
lexical_decisions.rationale: The negative is taken as governing the whole participial phrase, with ὄντας as the object of εἰδώς. Immediate attachment to ὄντας would instead yield the paradoxical alternative “knowing those who do not exist.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: silence and oblivion
lexical_decisions.rationale: λήθη here denotes the state of being forgotten rather than merely a personal lapse of memory.

passages.text: Continually pondering these and similar things—I do not know from where—I bore a painful grief so intense that I grew pale and wasted away. Most terrible of all, if ever I resolved to push the concern away as useless, my distress became all the more acute. I was troubled by this, not knowing that I had a noble thought as my housemate, one that would become for me a cause of good immortality, as I later learned by experience and gave thanks to God, the master of all. For the thought that oppressed me at first compelled me to enter upon the investigation and discovery of realities; and then I pronounced wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of calling blessed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὀδυνηρὰν εἶχον λύπην τοσοῦτον ὡς ὠχριακότα με τήκεσθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: I bore a painful grief so intense that I grew pale and wasted away
lexical_decisions.rationale: Expresses the result construction while retaining both pallor and physical wasting.

lexical_decisions.chosen: I had a noble thought as my housemate
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the domestic image of σύνοικον rather than reducing it to a thought merely being present.

lexical_decisions.chosen: one that would become for me a cause of good immortality
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains ἀγαθῆς, which qualifies the immortality positively rather than asserting immortality without qualification.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν τῶν πραγμάτων ζήτησιν καὶ εὕρεσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the investigation and discovery of realities
lexical_decisions.rationale: τὰ πράγματα denotes the matters or realities under philosophical investigation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐταλάνιζον οὓς τὴν ἀρχὴν διὰ ἄγνοιαν μακαρίζειν ἐκινδύνευον
lexical_decisions.chosen: I pronounced wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of calling blessed
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the deliberate contrast between ταλανίζω and μακαρίζω.

passages.text: From childhood, then, while absorbed in such lines of reasoning, I used to attend the philosophers’ schools in order to learn something certain. I found nothing except refutations and confirmations of doctrines, disputes and rivalries, techniques of syllogisms, and inventions of premises. At one time the claim would prevail—say, for example—that the soul is immortal, and at another that it is mortal. Whenever, then, an argument prevailed that it was immortal, I rejoiced; but whenever one prevailed that it was mortal, I grieved. Yet I was more disheartened because I could not establish either alternative securely in my own mind. Nevertheless, I perceived that opinions about the theses were judged false or true on account of their defenders and did not appear as they stood in relation to truth. Having at last realized, then, that comprehension does not arise from the theses being defended, but that opinions are pronounced on the basis of those defending them, I was reeling still more amid these questions. Therefore I groaned from the depth of my soul. For I was neither capable of establishing anything securely nor able to shake off concern about such things, although I wanted to, as I said earlier. For when I ordered myself, more and more frequently, to be still, somehow—I do not know how—the thought of such things would slip in upon me unnoticed and with pleasure.

source_issues.source_quote: ἐμαυτῷ πυκνότερον ἡσυχάζειν ἐπιτάσσοντος
source_issues.issue: The genitive participle has no expressed genitive subject. A first-person subject is readily supplied from ἐμαυτῷ and the context, though the construction may also be described as loose or anacoluthic. No emendation is required for a defensible translation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰς τὰς τῶν φιλοσόφων ἐφοίτων διατριβάς
lexical_decisions.chosen: I used to attend the philosophers’ schools
lexical_decisions.rationale: διατριβαί can denote lectures, discussions, or schools; “schools” conveys the recurring instructional setting.

lexical_decisions.chosen: refutations and confirmations of doctrines
lexical_decisions.rationale: The paired rhetorical terms denote arguments against and arguments establishing or supporting positions.

lexical_decisions.chosen: inventions of premises
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this logical context λήμματα are assumptions or premises used in argument.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αἱ δόξαι τῶν ὑποθέσεων παρὰ τοὺς ἐκδικοῦντας ψευδεῖς ἢ ἀληθεῖς ὑπολαμβάνονται
lexical_decisions.chosen: opinions about the theses were judged false or true on account of their defenders
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐκδικεῖν here means to champion or defend a position, while παρά with the accusative identifies the defenders as the basis of the judgment.

lexical_decisions.chosen: did not appear as they stood in relation to truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase is compressed; it can also be understood as “did not appear according to the truth they possessed.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἔτι μᾶλλον ἰλιγγίων ἐν τοῖς πράγμασιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: I was reeling still more amid these questions
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἰλιγγίων is treated as a finite first-person imperfect, presenting the increased reeling as the result of his realization rather than subordinating it to the following groaning.

lexical_decisions.chosen: when I ordered myself, more and more frequently, to be still
lexical_decisions.rationale: The first-person subject of the genitive participle is implicit but recoverable from ἐμαυτῷ and the surrounding narration.

passages.text: And again, at a loss, I would say to myself, “Why am I laboring for nothing? The matter is clear: if, once dead, I do not exist, it is not fitting for me to grieve while I now exist. So I will save grieving for that time, when, since I do not exist, I will not grieve. But if perhaps I do exist as something, grieving now is needless for me.” Immediately after this, another thought would enter me, for I would say, “Unless indeed I am destined to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now, if I have not lived devoutly, and, according to the accounts of some philosophers, I shall be handed over to Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus, like Sisyphus or Tityus or Ixion or Tantalus, and I will be in Hades, punished forever.” Again I would object in response, saying, “But these things are not real.” And again I would say, “But what if they are?” “Since the matter is uncertain, then,” I would say, “it is safer for me to live devoutly instead. And how will I be able, for the sake of what is right, while looking toward an uncertain hope, to master the body’s pleasures? But I am not even fully assured what exactly is right and pleasing to God; neither do I know whether the soul is immortal or mortal, nor do I know what certain argument can be found, nor can I rest from such thoughts.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τηρήσω τὸ λυπεῖσθαι εἰς τὴν τότε
lexical_decisions.chosen: I will save grieving for that time
lexical_decisions.rationale: The feminine article substantivizes an implied time or occasion; the paradox is that he will then be unable to grieve.

lexical_decisions.chosen: if perhaps I do exist as something
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the indefinite τι and the possibility that some form of existence continues after death.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Εἰ μήτι γε τοῦ νῦν με λυποῦντος ἐκεῖ χεῖρον παθεῖν ἔχω
lexical_decisions.chosen: Unless indeed I am destined to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now
lexical_decisions.rationale: εἰ μήτι γε introduces an exception to the preceding claim; in context it could also be expressed rhetorically as “What if indeed...?”

lexical_decisions.chosen: if I have not lived devoutly
lexical_decisions.rationale: The surrounding hypothetical fear supports a conditional rendering of the circumstantial perfect participle. The less resolved “not having lived devoutly” and the causal “because I have not lived devoutly” remain possible; the causal reading would present deficient conduct as assumed within the feared scenario rather than merely conditional.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus
lexical_decisions.rationale: The mythological names are transliterated without replacing them with generalized descriptions.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in Hades, punished forever
lexical_decisions.rationale: The accusative of duration τὸν αἰῶνα denotes punishment continuing through the age; “for the age” is a more formally literal alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: for the sake of what is right
lexical_decisions.rationale: The substantivized adjective refers to right or just conduct rather than introducing a separate named doctrine of righteousness.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τί ποτε ἔστιν δίκαιον ἀρέσκον θεῷ πεπληροφόρημαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: I am not even fully assured what exactly is right and pleasing to God
lexical_decisions.rationale: πεπληροφόρημαι expresses settled or full assurance, and ἀρέσκον θεῷ qualifies what is right.

lexical_decisions.chosen: nor do I know what certain argument can be found
lexical_decisions.rationale: The printed τίς is interrogative, and the clause is taken as a second indirect question governed by γινώσκω, parallel to the preceding question whether the soul is immortal or mortal. This preserves an epistemic limitation rather than asserting that no certain argument exists.

passages.text:
What, then, must be done except this? I will travel to Egypt, befriend the hierophants and prophets of the inner sanctuaries, and, after seeking and finding a magician, persuade him with a large sum of money to perform a sending up of a soul—the practice called necromancy—while I make an inquiry as though about some particular matter. But the inquiry will be about learning whether the soul is immortal. I will know the soul’s answer—that it is immortal—not because it has spoken or I have even heard it, but merely because it has appeared, so that, having seen it with my own eyes, I may have a self-sufficient and adequate conclusion from its mere appearance that it exists. The obscure words that belong to hearing will then no longer be able to overturn the eyes’ own evidence.

Nevertheless, I put this very plan before a philosopher of my acquaintance, who advised me in many ways not to dare it. “For if the soul does not heed the magician,” he said, “you will have acted against the laws that forbid people to do such things, and you will live with a guilty conscience. But if it does heed him, then, besides your living with a guilty conscience, I think you will no longer make progress in piety, for whose sake you even dared this. For they say that the divine is hostile toward those who harass souls at the dissolution of dead bodies.” When I heard this, I became more hesitant to undertake such a thing, but I did not abandon my original intention. Instead, I grew despondent, as though my impulse had been obstructed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a sending up of a soul—the practice called necromancy
lexical_decisions.rationale: “Sending up” preserves the directional image of ἀναπομπή rather than replacing it with the broader “summoning”; the parenthetical identification is retained.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐκ ἐκ τοῦ λαλῆσαι ἢ καὶ ἀκοῦσαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: not because it has spoken or I have even heard it
lexical_decisions.rationale: The infinitives do not state their subjects. Context supports the soul as speaker and Clement as hearer; the more impersonal “not from speaking or even hearing” is also grammatically possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a self-sufficient and adequate conclusion
lexical_decisions.rationale: Here ἀπόφασις denotes a determination or conclusion, not the unrelated sense “denial.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν ἴδια τὰ τῆς ἀκοῆς ἀνατρέψαι ἄδηλα ῥήματα
lexical_decisions.chosen: The obscure words that belong to hearing will then no longer be able to overturn the eyes’ own evidence
lexical_decisions.rationale: The obscure words are the grammatical agent, and what belongs to the eyes is the object. “Evidence” makes the substantival τὰ … ἴδια intelligible without changing the contrast between sight and hearing.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you will live with a guilty conscience
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adverb denotes living with a bad or troubled conscience, not merely living unhappily.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῖς τῇ λύσει θανόντων σωμάτων σκύλλουσιν τὰς ψυχάς
lexical_decisions.chosen: those who harass souls at the dissolution of dead bodies
lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative τῇ λύσει is read temporally or circumstantially, without making the harassers the explicit agents of the dissolution. “Through the dissolution of dead bodies” is a viable instrumental alternative. Reading λύσις as the release of souls from bodies is possible in context, but the supplied construction does not itself explicitly say that the necromancers release them.

passages.text: And, so that I may not recount such matters to you at great length, while I was occupied with so many reflections and circumstances, a certain report arose quietly during the reign of Tiberius Caesar. Beginning at the spring equinox, it continually grew and, truly a good messenger of God, ran throughout the world, unable to keep silent and conceal God’s will. It therefore became more widespread and greater each time, saying that a certain man in Judea, having begun at the spring equinox, was announcing to the Jews the good news of the kingdom of the everlasting God. He said that any one of them would enjoy it if he first set his way of life right. And to secure belief in him—that he did these things while full of divinity—he performed many marvelous signs and wonders by command alone, as one who had received authority from God. For he made the deaf hear and the blind see again; he made those with deformed limbs walk and set the lame upright; he drove away every disease and put every demon to flight. Even people with leprosy or scabies were healed and went away merely by fixing their gaze on him from a distance. Dead people brought to him were raised, and there was nothing he was unable to do. Indeed, the further time advanced, the far greater and more firmly established became—not the report any longer, I mean, but the truth of the matter—because of the increasing number of visitors. Assemblies were already forming in various places for deliberation and inquiry into who the one who had appeared might be and what he meant to say.

source_issues.source_quote: Ἰουδαίοις τὴν. τοῦ ἀιδίου θεοῦ
source_issues.issue: The printed full stop interrupts the article and its dependent genitive, where it cannot function as normal sentence punctuation. The translation provisionally treats it as intrusive editorial punctuation while preserving all the printed words.

lexical_decisions.chosen: at the spring equinox
lexical_decisions.rationale: τροπή can denote a seasonal turning point, including an equinox. “At the turn of spring” is a less technically specific alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς ἀληθῶς ἀγαθὴ θεοῦ ἄγγελος διέτρεχε τὸν κόσμον
lexical_decisions.chosen: truly a good messenger of God, ran throughout the world
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὡς ἀληθῶς is taken idiomatically as “truly” or “in truth,” affirming the report’s personification rather than introducing a comparison. ἄγγελος retains the ordinary sense “messenger”; “angel of God” is lexically possible but would make the personification more specifically supernatural.

lexical_decisions.chosen: first set his way of life right
lexical_decisions.rationale: πολιτεία here concerns conduct or manner of life, while προ- supplies the prior action required before enjoying the kingdom.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ δὲ πιστεύεσθαι αὐτὸν χάριν ὅτι θειότητος γέμων ταῦτα ποιεῖ
lexical_decisions.chosen: to secure belief in him—that he did these things while full of divinity
lexical_decisions.rationale: The ὅτι clause is treated as the content to be believed. It can alternatively be read causally: “to secure belief in him, because he does these things while full of divinity.” “Full of divine power” is a possible contextual rendering of θειότης, but “divinity” preserves the source’s stronger wording.

lexical_decisions.chosen: he made those with deformed limbs walk and set the lame upright
lexical_decisions.rationale: The translation preserves the source’s distinction between κυλλοί, people with bent or deformed limbs, and χωλοί, the lame.

lexical_decisions.chosen: people with leprosy or scabies
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main rendering reads the juxtaposed adjectives as two groups within the surrounding enumeration of afflictions: λεπροί as people with leprosy and ψωροί as people with a scabby or mangy skin condition, here rendered “scabies.” Because there is no conjunction, the words can alternatively describe one group as both leprous and scabby: “scabby leprous people.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: because of the increasing number of visitors
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπιδημέω describes people visiting or sojourning in a place. “Through more of those arriving” is a more literal alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Assemblies … in various places
lexical_decisions.rationale: συστήματα can denote organized groups, gatherings, or assemblies; the following deliberation and inquiry favor “assemblies.”

passages.text:
And indeed, once in that very year, at the autumn equinox, someone stood up publicly and shouted, saying, “Men of Rome, listen! The Son of God is present in Judea, promising eternal life to all who desire it, if they live according to the intention of the Father who sent him. Therefore change your way—from worse things to better, from temporary things to eternal. Recognize that there is one God, the heavenly one, whose world you inhabit unjustly before his righteous eyes. But if you make this change and live according to his will, you will be carried into another age, become everlasting, and enjoy his ineffable good things. If, however, you disobey, your souls will be cast, after the dissolution of the body, into the place of fire, where, while being punished eternally, they will reorient themselves to no avail. For each person’s present life is the time for reorientation.”

As I listened to this, I was distressed that no one from among such great crowds, after hearing so momentous an announcement, had said, “I will travel to Judea so that I may see whether this man is telling the truth when he says these things.” For the claim was that the Son of God had come to Judea and, for the sake of a good and eternal hope, was revealing the will of the Father who sent him—especially since what they say he proclaims is no small matter. For he confidently affirms that the souls of some, being eternal, will enjoy eternal good things, while the souls of others, cast into unquenchable fire, will be punished throughout the age.

source_issues.source_quote: μετὰ τὴν τοῦ σώματος·λύσιν
source_issues.issue: The printed middle dot falls inside the article-genitive-noun phrase and interrupts “the dissolution of the body.” The translation provisionally treats it as intrusive editorial punctuation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in that very year
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase locates the event at or close upon the same year. “About that same year” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: at the autumn equinox
lexical_decisions.rationale: As with the corresponding spring expression, τροπή denotes a seasonal turning point; “at the turn of autumn” is a broader alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: change your way
lexical_decisions.rationale: The wording calls for a change in manner or way of life. It is kept distinct from the μετανοέω word group later in the passage.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀνωφέλητα μετανοήσουσιν· ὁ γὰρ τῆς μετανοίας καιρὸς
lexical_decisions.chosen: they will reorient themselves to no avail. For … the time for reorientation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The cognate verb and noun are rendered consistently under the supplied terminology policy. “They will repent uselessly … the time for repentance” is the traditional alternative; “they will regret it to no avail” would emphasize their futile response under punishment.

lexical_decisions.chosen: his ineffable good things
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀπόρρητος can mean secret, forbidden to disclose, or unutterable. “Ineffable” fits the transcendent benefits here while preserving their unspeakable character.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς ὅτι υἱὸς θεοῦ ἐπιδεδήμηκεν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: For the claim was that the Son of God had come to Judea
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὡς ὅτι can introduce reported content or give a causal explanation. The context of a public report favors reported content; “since indeed the Son of God had come” is a viable alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Son of God
lexical_decisions.rationale: Although the phrase is anarthrous here, it refers contextually to the previously identified ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ υἱός. “A son of God” remains grammatically possible if the phrase is read indefinitely.

lexical_decisions.chosen: will be punished throughout the age
lexical_decisions.rationale: This preserves the explicit noun αἰών rather than automatically assimilating it to the nearby ἀϊδίως. In this context “will be punished forever” is also semantically supportable.

passages.text: While saying these things about others, I also spoke to myself: “Why do I blame others when I am under the same charge of negligence? No, I will set out for Judea after first arranging my own affairs.” Yet although I had resolved on this course, a long period of delay followed, because the affairs of life were difficult to disentangle. At last, then, I somehow reflected on the nature of life: by entangling those who are eager in hope, it lies in wait for them. Moreover, I reflected on how long I had been stealthily drawn in while being tossed about by hopes, and on the fact that we human beings die while occupied in this way. Leaving all my affairs just as they happened to be, I hurried to Portus. After reaching the harbor and putting out to sea, I was carried by the winds’ hostility to Alexandria instead of Judea. Held there for lack of winds, I spent time with the philosophers and recounted the accounts concerning both the report and the man who had appeared in Rome. They replied, “We do not know the man who appeared in Rome. But about the one who had been in Judea and whom the report calls the Son of God, we have also heard from many who have come from there as well, and we have learned about all the wonders he performed by speaking.”

source_issues.source_quote: οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ. ὃν ποτε
source_issues.issue: The printed full stop separates καί from the following relative construction, leaving the latter as an abrupt fragment. The translation provisionally treats the stop as intrusive editorial punctuation while retaining the difficult wording that follows.
source_issues.proposed_reading: οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ ὃν ποτε

source_issues.source_quote: ὃν ποτε εἰσεκλάπην χρόνον ἐλπίσιν δονούμενος
source_issues.issue: The supplied wording is lexically and syntactically unusual but is retained unchanged. The translation provisionally reads χρόνον as an accusative of duration and εἰσεκλάπην with passive inward or surreptitious-entry force. An intransitive understanding such as “had slipped in unnoticed” remains possible; no conjectural correction is proposed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: after first arranging my own affairs
lexical_decisions.rationale: διατίθημι with βίος can refer to putting one’s life in order. The following practical delays favor arranging personal affairs rather than an exclusively moral sense.

lexical_decisions.chosen: I somehow reflected on the nature of life
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὡδίποτε is taken adverbially as “somehow or other.” The unusual expression is intelligible without conjectural alteration.

lexical_decisions.chosen: by entangling those who are eager in hope, it lies in wait for them
lexical_decisions.rationale: Life remains the implied subject of both participle and verb. “Those who hurry” is the more literal alternative for τοὺς σπεύδοντας.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὃν ποτε εἰσεκλάπην χρόνον ἐλπίσιν δονούμενος
lexical_decisions.chosen: how long I had been stealthily drawn in while being tossed about by hopes
lexical_decisions.rationale: The accusative ὃν … χρόνον is read as duration and represented by “how long,” rather than as the direct object of εἰσεκλάπην. The verb is given its inward and surreptitious force as “had been stealthily drawn in.” “Had slipped in unnoticed” is possible if the passive form is understood intransitively, while “had been inveigled” is another contextual possibility; the destination or situation entered is not expressed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to Portus
lexical_decisions.rationale: The capitalized Πόρτον is treated as Portus, Rome’s harbor settlement, rather than translated generically as “to the port.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: by the winds’ hostility
lexical_decisions.rationale: This preserves the source’s personifying image rather than reducing the phrase to “because of adverse winds.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ τῆς φήμης καὶ τοῦ ἐν Ῥώμῃ φανέντος ἔλεγον τοὺς λόγους
lexical_decisions.chosen: recounted the accounts concerning both the report and the man who had appeared in Rome
lexical_decisions.rationale: The syntax is somewhat redundant, but λόγους can denote accounts concerning both topics. “Related what the report said and the words of the man” is possible, though it more strongly makes the second genitive possessive.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ γενομένου καὶ υἱοῦ θεοῦ ὑπὸ τῆς φήμης λεγομένου
lexical_decisions.chosen: the one who had been in Judea and whom the report calls the Son of God
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὑπὸ τῆς φήμης explicitly identifies the report as the source of the designation “Son of God.” The broader γενομένου is rendered neutrally as “had been”; “had appeared” or “had emerged” is possible in context.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ παρὰ πολλῶν τῶν κἀκεῖθεν ἐληλυθότων ἠκούσαμεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: we have also heard from many who have come from there as well
lexical_decisions.rationale: The additive wording is retained without supplying an unexpressed first source for ἠκούσαμεν. That first point of comparison could be Clement’s account or another source; ὑπὸ τῆς φήμης belongs explicitly to the preceding designation, not necessarily to the verb “we have heard.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: the wonders he performed by speaking
lexical_decisions.rationale: The circumstantial participle λαλῶν can express means, yielding miracles performed by speech. “The wonders he performed while speaking” is also grammatically possible.

passages.text: When I said, “I would like to meet someone among those who had seen him,” they immediately led me away, saying, “There is someone here who has not only become personally acquainted with him but is also from the land there—a Hebrew man named Barnabas. He also says that he is one of his disciples, and, sitting somewhere around here, he readily tells those who wish to hear the words of that man’s promise.” So I went along with them. When I arrived, I stood with the crowd that was present, listening to his words, and I realized that he was speaking the truth, not by dialectical skill, but was setting out without guile and without preparation both what he had heard and what he had seen the Son of God who had appeared do and say. He also supplied, from the very crowd then present, many witnesses for both the wonders and the words he was recounting.

source_issues.source_quote: ἑορακότων
source_issues.issue: This is a non-Attic or later perfect form of ὁράω rather than the classical-looking ἑωρακότων. The same passage later prints ἑόρακεν, supporting an orthographic pattern rather than an unreadable source. The meaning is secure, and the printed form is not emended in the translation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: I would like to meet someone
lexical_decisions.rationale: The imperfect ἤθελον can express a polite or tentative desire; “I wanted to meet” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: who has not only become personally acquainted with him
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἱστορέω with a person can mean visiting or gaining firsthand acquaintance, not merely collecting information. “Who has visited him” or “who has investigated him” are possible but less responsive to Clement’s request to meet an eyewitness.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the words of that man’s promise
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὑπόσχεσις denotes a promise or undertaking. The demonstrative is retained rather than replaced with a named referent.

lexical_decisions.chosen: without guile and without preparation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves both Barnabas’s lack of deceit or artifice and the extemporaneous character of his presentation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Son of God who had appeared
lexical_decisions.rationale: φανέντα describes the Son as having appeared or become manifest; the wording does not itself specify how that appearance is to be understood.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ λεγομένων θαυμασίων τε καὶ λόγων
lexical_decisions.chosen: for both the wonders and the words he was recounting
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive identifies what the witnesses attest. αὐτοῦ most naturally refers to Barnabas as the one recounting them, though the words and wonders themselves concern the appeared Son.

passages.text: But because the crowds were favorably disposed toward what was being said without guile, the philosophers who came from a worldly education began laughing at him and jeering at him, making jokes and deriding him with immeasurable insolence, as though they were wielding syllogisms as mighty weapons. He, however, thrust aside their nonsense and did not join in their crafty questioning; instead, undaunted, he continued speaking without stopping. Once someone asked him why a gnat came into being and, though extremely small, has six feet and also wings, whereas the elephant, the largest of animals, though wingless, has only four feet. After the question, he took up the discourse that had been interrupted. As his answer to the question, he resumed the discourse that had been before him from the beginning, using only the following preface after each interruption: “We have been commanded only to tell you the words and marvelous deeds of the one who sent us. Instead of a logical demonstration, we offer you many witnesses from among you who are present, whose faces I remember as living images and sufficient testimonies. From this point it is within your power to yield or to disobey. But I will not cease telling you what benefits you, because silence is loss to me, while disobedience is harm to you. I could also supply demonstrations in answer to your groundless challenges, if you were asking with love for truth. But it is not timely now to tell you, who are ignorant of the God of all things, the reason for the differing creation of the gnat and the elephant.”

source_issues.source_quote: ἐπειδὴ δὲ πρὸς τὰ ἀπανούργως λεγόμενα· ἡδέως οἱ ὄχλοι διετίθεντο
source_issues.issue: The printed middle point after λεγόμενα interrupts the ἐπειδή clause even though ἡδέως οἱ ὄχλοι διετίθεντο supplies its finite verb. This appears to be editorial punctuation rather than missing wording, and the translation construes the clause continuously.
source_issues.proposed_reading: ἐπειδὴ δὲ πρὸς τὰ ἀπανούργως λεγόμενα ἡδέως οἱ ὄχλοι διετίθεντο,

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸς τὰ ἀπανούργως λεγόμενα· ἡδέως οἱ ὄχλοι διετίθεντο
lexical_decisions.chosen: the crowds were favorably disposed toward what was being said without guile
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἡδέως διετίθεντο describes a favorable or pleased response, while ἀπανούργως emphasizes the absence of craftiness.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ συνέτρεχεν αὐτῶν τῇ πανούργῳ πεύσει
lexical_decisions.chosen: did not join in their crafty questioning
lexical_decisions.rationale: The literal image is that he did not “run together with” their questioning. The English expresses his refusal to follow them into their contrived line of inquiry.

lexical_decisions.chosen: he took up the discourse that had been interrupted
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐμποδίζω here describes the discourse as impeded by the question, and ἀναλαμβάνω marks its resumption.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς πρὸς τὴν πεῦσιν ἀποκρινάμενος τὸν αὐτῷ ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς προκείμενον ἀνελάμβανεν λόγον
lexical_decisions.chosen: As his answer to the question, he resumed the discourse that had been before him from the beginning
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main rendering treats his resumption of the discourse as his response to the question, fitting the following statement that he repeatedly used the same preface when interrupted. Because ὡς with the aorist participle may instead mark assumed posture or manner, the clause can also be rendered, “As though he had answered the question, he resumed the discourse that had been before him from the beginning.” On that reading, the narrator does not present the resumed discourse straightforwardly as an answer, but describes Barnabas as proceeding as one who had answered.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὧν ἐγὼ τὰ εἴδη μέμνημαι ὡς ἐμψύχους εἰκόνας ἱκανὰς μαρτυρίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: whose faces I remember as living images and sufficient testimonies
lexical_decisions.rationale: εἴδη can mean forms, appearances, or faces. “Faces” suits remembered eyewitnesses; “whose forms I remember” remains possible. The appositional language treats those remembered appearances as living images and adequate testimony.

lexical_decisions.chosen: your groundless challenges
lexical_decisions.rationale: εἰκαῖος can describe what is random, purposeless, or without sound basis, while προβλήματα are questions or challenges put forward. “Your random questions” is a viable alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you, who are ignorant of the God of all things
lexical_decisions.rationale: τῶν ὅλων belongs with θεόν and identifies God as God of the totality, not merely as a god unknown in some limited respect.

passages.text: As he was saying these things, they let loose disorderly laughter as though by common agreement, trying to silence him and leave him at a loss, as though he were some raving barbarian. When I saw this, I was seized—I do not know how—with zeal and pious indignation. I could no longer endure remaining silent, but cried out boldly, saying: “With good reason God has made his will incomprehensible to you, foreseeing that you were unworthy, as is now evident from the very things by which he fully convinces those who possess discerning minds. For heralds of his will have now been sent out, not professing grammatical art, but displaying his will in simple and guileless words, so that absolutely anyone, upon hearing, understands what is being said, and not with some grudging polish that is unwilling to make itself available to everyone. Yet here you are: besides not understanding what benefits you, you laugh, to your own harm, at the truth that has lived as a citizen among barbarians—to your condemnation. Though it has now visited even you, you do not wish to receive it as a guest, because of your wanton conduct and the plainness of its words, so that you may not be exposed as people who are lovers of words to no purpose and not philosophers who love truth. How long, then, will you keep learning to talk, you who do not know how to speak well? For many utterances from you are not worth one word. What, then, will your Greek multitude say, once it has become one soul, if there is indeed to be a judgment, as this man says? ‘Why, God, did you not proclaim your will to us?’ Will you not surely hear—if indeed you are deemed worthy of an answer—the following? ‘I knew, before the foundation of the world, every choice that would be made, and secretly went beforehand to meet each person according to what that person deserved. But wishing to give those who have taken refuge with me full assurance of this very fact—that it is so, and why I did not allow my will to be proclaimed publicly from the beginning, starting with earlier generations—I have now, near the end of life, sent heralds of my counsel. They are laughed at and, while being insulted, are mocked by people who wish to receive no benefit and who have forcefully rejected my friendship. Oh, the magnitude of the injustice! Heralds risk being murdered, and this at the hands of men who are being called to salvation!’”

lexical_decisions.chosen: as though he were some raving barbarian
lexical_decisions.rationale: δαιμονάω can suggest being possessed or behaving madly. “Raving” preserves the hostile characterization without deciding whether the mockers meant literal possession.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ζήλῳ οὐκ οἶδ’ ὅπως ληφθεὶς εὐσεβεῖ θυμῷ
lexical_decisions.chosen: seized—I do not know how—with zeal and pious indignation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The two datival expressions describe Clement’s impelling zeal and religiously framed passion or anger. θυμός could also be rendered “ardor” or “anger.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς ἐξ ὧν νῦν τοὺς κριτικὸν νοῦν ἔχοντας πληροφορῶν φαίνεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: as is now evident from the very things by which he fully convinces those who possess discerning minds
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering takes φαίνεται impersonally in English and treats ἐξ ὧν as the evidentiary basis by which God convinces discerning people. Alternatively, the phrase may mean that God’s present convincing of discerning people is itself what makes the hearers’ unworthiness apparent.

lexical_decisions.chosen: not professing grammatical art
lexical_decisions.rationale: γραμματικὴ τέχνη refers to educated literary or grammatical expertise. The relatively literal wording preserves the contrast with the heralds’ simple speech.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ μετὰ ξέσεώς τινος φθονερᾶς, παρέχειν πᾶσιν ἑαυτὴν μὴ βουλομένης
lexical_decisions.chosen: not with some grudging polish that is unwilling to make itself available to everyone
lexical_decisions.rationale: ξέσις is literally a scraping or polishing and here depicts refined rhetorical finish. The feminine participle most directly agrees with ξέσεως, personifying such refinement as grudgingly inaccessible; it could alternatively be understood more broadly of an elitist mode of presentation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν εἰς τὴν ὑμετέραν καταδίκην ἐν βαρβάροις πολιτευσαμένην ἀλήθειαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the truth that has lived as a citizen among barbarians—to your condemnation
lexical_decisions.rationale: πολιτεύομαι carries civic imagery: truth has conducted its life or held citizenship among those the Greeks call barbarians. The following ξενίσαι continues the contrasting guest imagery.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰκῇ φιλόλογοί ἐστε καὶ οὐ φιλαληθεῖς φιλόσοφοι
lexical_decisions.chosen: you are lovers of words to no purpose and not philosophers who love truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: The wording preserves the author’s contrast and wordplay between φιλόλογοι, φιλαληθεῖς, and φιλόσοφοι. εἰκῇ marks their devotion to words as vain or purposeless.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Will you not surely hear
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this rhetorical question πάντως is taken affirmatively as “surely” or “certainly.” In a declarative setting οὐ πάντως could instead mean “not altogether” or “not necessarily,” but that reading fits the present question poorly.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πάσας τὰς ἐσομένας πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου εἰδὼς προαιρέσεις
lexical_decisions.chosen: I knew, before the foundation of the world, every choice that would be made
lexical_decisions.rationale: προαίρεσις can denote a choice, purpose, or moral disposition. “Choice” preserves the emphasis on acts or orientations of volition without adding a developed theory of free will.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦτο δὲ αὐτὸ ὅτι οὕτως ἔχει βουληθεὶς τοὺς προσπεφευγότας μοι πληροφορήσαι διὰ τί
lexical_decisions.chosen: wishing to give those who have taken refuge with me full assurance of this very fact—that it is so, and why
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering treats ὅτι οὕτως ἔχει and the following διὰ τί clause as coordinated content of πληροφορήσαι. It is also possible to construe the wording more tightly as assurance precisely about why matters stand this way.

lexical_decisions.chosen: near the end of life
lexical_decisions.rationale: βίος literally denotes life or its course. In this universal historical context it may refer more broadly to the close of the present course of worldly life, but “age” or “world” is not explicitly written.

lexical_decisions.chosen: who have forcefully rejected my friendship
lexical_decisions.rationale: παραιτέομαι means declining, refusing, or rejecting, and ἐπιτεταμένως gives the refusal an emphatic or strenuous character.

passages.text: “‘This injustice being committed against my heralds would have been committed against everyone from the beginning, if the unworthy had been called to salvation from the beginning. For what they now do unjustly serves as a defense of my just providence: I rightly did not wish, from the beginning, to expose publicly to abuse, and to no benefit, the message worthy of honor. Instead, I resolved that it should be kept unspoken as something precious—not withheld from those who were worthy from the beginning, for I did share it with them, but from these people and others like them, who, as you see, are unworthy, who hate me and do not wish to love themselves.’ And now, at any rate, stop laughing at this man. Question me about his proclamation, or let anyone who wishes answer me when I question him. Do not bark like wanton dogs, shutting the ears of those who wish to be saved with disorderly noise. You unjust people, hateful to God and turning the reasoning that saves aside into unbelief, how can you obtain pardon when you insult the man who offers to tell you about God’s divine nature—and that too a man whom you ought to have welcomed because of his good intention toward you, even if he said nothing true?”

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ νῦν γε παρέντες· γελᾶν τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸ τούτου ἐπάγγελμα πυνθάνεσθε
source_issues.issue: The printed middle point after παρέντες separates the participle from the infinitive γελᾶν, although παρέντες γελᾶν gives the defensible sense “stop laughing.” The translation treats the punctuation as editorial and construes ἐμοῦ with πυνθάνεσθε, “question me.” No wording is supplied or removed.
source_issues.proposed_reading: καὶ νῦν γε, παρέντες γελᾶν τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον, ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸ τούτου ἐπάγγελμα πυνθάνεσθε

lexical_decisions.chosen: the message worthy of honor
lexical_decisions.rationale: λόγος here is the proclaimed teaching or message rather than merely an individual word. “The discourse worthy of honor” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to expose publicly to abuse
lexical_decisions.rationale: The literal construction is to “place” the message publicly into insult or outrage. “Expose publicly to abuse” conveys both the placement and its intended result.

lexical_decisions.chosen: it should be kept unspoken as something precious
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive σιγᾶσθαι means that the message is to be kept silent or left unspoken, while τίμιον can mean precious, highly valued, or honorable.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐκ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἀξίων (οἷς καὶ μετέδωκα), ἀλλὰ ἀπὸ τούτων καὶ τῶν τοιούτων
lexical_decisions.chosen: not withheld from those who were worthy from the beginning, for I did share it with them, but from these people and others like them
lexical_decisions.rationale: The repeated ἀπό depends on the idea of being kept unspoken from particular groups. “Withheld” makes that relation idiomatic without supplying any missing content.

lexical_decisions.chosen: about his proclamation
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπάγγελμα can mean a declaration, profession, undertaking, claim, or promise. Here it denotes what Barnabas publicly professes or proclaims; “about his claim” is a viable alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: bark like wanton dogs
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀσελγής may mean wanton, shameless, insolent, or undisciplined. “Wanton” preserves the severity of the insult without narrowing it to sexual misconduct.

lexical_decisions.chosen: hateful to God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound most naturally has a passive sense, “hated by” or “hateful to God,” and commonly characterizes the impious. “God-hating” is lexically possible if the compound is taken actively.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν σώζοντα λογισμὸν εἰς ἀπιστίαν ἀπασχολοῦντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: turning the reasoning that saves aside into unbelief
lexical_decisions.rationale: λογισμός is reasoning, reflection, or the rational faculty, and ἀπασχολέω describes diverting or preoccupying it. The phrase depicts their noise as redirecting potentially saving thought toward unbelief.

lexical_decisions.chosen: God’s divine nature
lexical_decisions.rationale: θειότης denotes divinity or divine nature. The rendering retains the source’s explicit genitive “of God” rather than replacing it with a different theological formulation.

passages.text: While I was saying these things and what followed from them, a great uproar arose among the crowds. Some, out of pity for Barnabas, took my side, but others, being foolish, fiercely gnashed their teeth at me. When evening had finally overtaken us, I took Barnabas by the hand and forcibly led him, though he was unwilling, to my house. There I also made him stay, so that no one might lay hands on him. After remaining for a few days and briefly instructing me in the word of truth—a little, given the few days—he said that he was hurrying to Judaea for the sake of the festival observed according to his religion, and he wanted from then on to be with his own fellow countrymen.

lexical_decisions.chosen: took my side
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expression indicates joining Clement in support of Barnabas; alternatives include “joined me” and the more literal “helped lift with me.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δεινῶς κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἔβρυχον τοὺς ὀδόντας
lexical_decisions.chosen: fiercely gnashed their teeth at me
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the hostile force of δεινῶς and the physical image of grinding or gnashing the teeth.

lexical_decisions.chosen: briefly instructing me
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατηχέω denotes oral instruction here; the context does not require the later technical sense of formal catechesis.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the festival observed according to his religion
lexical_decisions.rationale: This retains the passage’s characterization of the festival through θρησκεία without identifying or harmonizing it with a particular named observance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: his own fellow countrymen
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὁμοεθνής denotes people belonging to the same nation or ethnic community.

passages.text: But it was plain to me that he had become reluctant. For I said, “You need only set out for me the words you heard from the man who appeared, and I, after adorning them with my own discourse, will proclaim the will of God. Then, within a few days, I will sail with you, for I greatly long to reach the regions of Judaea. Perhaps I will even live with you for the entire course of my life.” But when he heard this, he answered, “If you wish to investigate our affairs and learn what is beneficial, sail with me at once. At any rate, today I will tell you the directions to my lodging and to those whom you wish to find, so that whenever you want, you may come and join us. For tomorrow I will depart for my own place.” And so, seeing that he was unyielding, I went with him as far as the harbor. After learning from him the directions to the residences that he had mentioned, I said to him, “If it were not that tomorrow I am to collect something owed to me, I would sail with you at once. Nevertheless, I will catch up with you very soon.” After saying this and entrusting him to the ship’s officers, I went back sorrowfully, thinking of my good and intimate friend.

source_issues.source_quote: ἐπεί γε τὰ σημεῖα τῆς οἰκήσεώς μου καὶ ὧν θέλεις ἐγώ σοι σήμερον ἐρῶ
source_issues.issue: The attachment and referent of ὧν θέλεις are ambiguous. The rendering takes it as referring to people whose identifying directions Clement wants, while alternatives include “the things you want” or treating the phrase as further information about Barnabas’s lodging. ἐπεί γε may be causal, “since indeed,” or transitional, “at any rate”; the latter is adopted contextually without treating the wording as defective.

lexical_decisions.chosen: But it was plain to me that he had become reluctant
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀποναρκάω can suggest becoming numb, indifferent, weary, or disinclined. “Reluctant” fits Barnabas’s refusal to remain and instruct Clement on Clement’s terms.

lexical_decisions.chosen: and I, after adorning them with my own discourse
lexical_decisions.rationale: κοσμέω retains the potentially self-confident claim that Clement would embellish or ornament the reported words with his own presentation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: sail with me at once
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this context ἐξ αὐτῆς functions idiomatically as “immediately” or “at once.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: investigate our affairs
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἱστορέω means to inquire into or learn by investigation, rather than merely to write a history.

lexical_decisions.chosen: And so, seeing that he was unyielding
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀδυσώπητος describes someone who cannot be moved by entreaty; “inexorable” is a possible but less accessible alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Εἰ μὴ ὅτι αὔριόν τι ἀπαιτῶ ὀφειλόμενόν μοι
lexical_decisions.chosen: If it were not that tomorrow I am to collect something owed to me
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀπαιτέω here means to demand or collect what is due, while τι leaves the precise object unspecified.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the ship’s officers
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase denotes those directing or commanding the vessel; alternatives include “leaders” and “captains.”

passages.text: After spending some days there and being unable to recover the debt in full, I disregarded what remained for the sake of speed, since it was an impediment, and I myself sailed to Judaea. After fifteen days I arrived at Caesarea of Straton. When I had set foot on land and was looking for lodging, I learned that a certain man called Peter—the most highly approved disciple of the man who had appeared in Judaea and had performed signs and wonders—was to hold a verbal debate the next day with Simon, the Samaritan from Gittha. When I heard this, I asked that Peter’s lodging be pointed out to me. I learned where it was and at the same time came to the gateway. When those in the house saw me, they questioned me about who I was and where I had come from. And behold, Barnabas came out and, as soon as he saw me, embraced me, rejoicing greatly and weeping. Taking me by the hand, he led me inside to where Peter was and said to me, “This is Peter, whom I declared to you to be greatest in the wisdom of God. I spoke to him about you continually, as you will learn for yourself, for I truthfully described everything about you as good and at the same time disclosed your resolve, with the result that he himself is eager to see you too. Therefore, through my own hands I present you to him as a great gift.” After saying this, he presented me and said, “This is Clement, Peter.”

source_issues.source_quote: τὸ χρέος οὐχ. ὅλον λαβεῖν δυνηθείς
source_issues.issue: The printed period after οὐχ interrupts the otherwise intelligible phrase “unable to receive the debt in full.” It is treated provisionally as anomalous editorial punctuation, not as missing content.
source_issues.proposed_reading: τὸ χρέος οὐχ ὅλον λαβεῖν δυνηθείς

source_issues.source_quote: τοῦ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα· πεποιηκότος
source_issues.issue: The printed middle dot separates the object σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα from πεποιηκότος, although the article τοῦ and participle naturally form the phrase “the one who had performed signs and wonders.” The translation treats the punctuation as non-syntactic; the supplied words remain intelligible.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ ὁμῶς ἔμαθον καὶ τῷ πυλῶνι ἐπέστην
source_issues.issue: The verified printed form is ὁμῶς, not concessive ὅμως. Its exact contribution is uncertain: it can express sameness, togetherness, or co-occurrence. The main text provisionally adopts temporal co-occurrence, “at the same time,” without altering the Greek; “together” or “likewise” remain possible but produce a less transparent relation between the two actions.

source_issues.source_quote: ἅμα καὶ τὴν προαίρεσιν ἐξέφανα, ὡς αὐτὸν γλίχεσθαι καὶ ἰδεῖν σε
source_issues.issue: The possessor of προαίρεσιν and the force of ὡς are ambiguous. The translation contextually understands the resolve as Clement’s and ὡς as introducing the result that Peter became eager to see him. Alternatively, the phrase may mean that Barnabas disclosed Peter’s inclination, namely that Peter himself was eager to see Clement.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τάχους ἕνεκα ἀμελήσας τοῦ περιλειφθέντος ὡς ἐμποδίου ὄντος
lexical_decisions.chosen: I disregarded what remained for the sake of speed, since it was an impediment
lexical_decisions.rationale: The remainder is the unpaid portion of the debt; the translation preserves Clement’s characterization of waiting for it as an obstacle.

lexical_decisions.chosen: I arrived at Caesarea of Straton
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive distinguishes the city conventionally known as Caesarea Maritima or Straton’s Caesarea without replacing the source’s wording.

lexical_decisions.chosen: was looking for lodging
lexical_decisions.rationale: θηράω literally evokes hunting or seeking; here its object ξενία indicates a search for lodging or hospitality.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the most highly approved disciple
lexical_decisions.rationale: δοκιμώτατος can mean most tested, approved, esteemed, or distinguished; “most highly approved” retains its superlative evaluative force.

lexical_decisions.chosen: was to hold a verbal debate
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expression denotes an examination or dispute conducted through words; alternatives include “discussion” and “debate of arguments.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ ὁμῶς ἔμαθον καὶ τῷ πυλῶνι ἐπέστην
lexical_decisions.chosen: I learned where it was and at the same time came to the gateway
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering takes the verified ὁμῶς as expressing co-occurrence rather than the concessive force associated with ὅμως. Alternatives include “together” or “in like manner,” though their precise application here is less clear.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀντέβαλλον τίς τε ὢν καὶ πόθεν ἥκω
lexical_decisions.chosen: they questioned me about who I was and where I had come from
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀντιβάλλω has the contextual sense of putting questions or statements to someone, not merely its literal sense of throwing one thing against another.

lexical_decisions.chosen: as you will learn for yourself
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase suggests knowledge arising directly or of itself from what occurs; alternatives include “from the event itself” and “directly.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅτι πάντα τὰ κατὰ σὲ καλὰ ὄντα ἀψευδῶς ἀντέβαλλον
lexical_decisions.chosen: for I truthfully described everything about you as good
lexical_decisions.rationale: The predicate-position καλὰ ὄντα supports the broader claim that everything concerning Clement was represented as good, rather than restricting the report only to a subset of good things.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through my own hands I present you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The wording preserves Barnabas’s image of personally presenting Clement as a gift.

passages.text: The good Peter sprang toward me as soon as he heard my name and kissed me warmly. After making me sit down, he immediately said, “You did well to host Barnabas, the herald of truth, nobly in honor of the true God, neither ashamed nor frightened by the anger of the uneducated crowds. You will be blessed. For just as you hosted the ambassador of truth with every honor, so truth itself will make you, though a stranger, a citizen of its own city. Then you will rejoice greatly because you have now lent a brief favor—meaning an inclination toward good discourses. You will be an heir of eternal and inalienable good things. And do not weary yourself describing your character to me, for Barnabas, who does not lie, has related everything about you to us, making favorable mention of you almost every day. To tell you briefly, as a genuine friend, what lies before us: if nothing hinders you, travel with us and share in the discourses of truth that I am about to deliver city by city, all the way to Rome itself. And you too, if there is anything you wish, speak.”

source_issues.source_quote: προαίρεσιν λόγων καλῶν λέγων
source_issues.issue: The parenthetical expression is semantically and syntactically compressed. The rendering takes λόγων καλῶν as an objective genitive, “an inclination toward good discourses,” while alternatives include “a preference for good discourses,” “a resolve for good words,” and “a good disposition expressed in words.” The speaker-neutral “meaning” allows λέγων either to function as a narrative explanation of Peter’s meaning or as Peter’s own parenthetical clarification; the supplied punctuation does not uniquely settle that presentation.

source_issues.source_quote: ξένον ὄντα τῆς ἰδίας πόλεως καταστήσει πολίτην
source_issues.issue: The genitive τῆς ἰδίας πόλεως can attach primarily to ξένον, “a stranger to its own city,” or to πολίτην, “a citizen of its own city.” The main rendering adopts the latter attachment while preserving the stranger-citizen contrast.

lexical_decisions.chosen: kissed me warmly
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compound verb can indicate affectionate or repeated kissing; “warmly” conveys its intensity without specifying an unsupported number of kisses.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in honor of the true God
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὄντως qualifies θεοῦ as genuinely or really God. Alternatives include “the real God” and “the one who truly is God”; the phrase does not by itself make bare existence a separate predicate.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the ambassador of truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρεσβευτής denotes an authorized envoy or ambassador; “messenger” is possible but less specific.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ξένον ὄντα τῆς ἰδίας πόλεως καταστήσει πολίτην
lexical_decisions.chosen: will make you, though a stranger, a citizen of its own city
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves the contrast between ξένος and πολίτης and attaches τῆς ἰδίας πόλεως primarily to “citizen.” It can alternatively be heard with “stranger.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: you have now lent a brief favor
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐδάνεισας preserves the metaphor of lending, while βραχεῖαν may describe the favor as brief or small; “brief” suits the contrast with eternal benefits.

lexical_decisions.chosen: eternal and inalienable good things
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀναφαίρετος describes what cannot be taken away; alternatives include “irrevocable” and “unremovable.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μὴ κάμνε ἀντιβάλλειν μοι τὸ σὸν ἦθος
lexical_decisions.chosen: do not weary yourself describing your character to me
lexical_decisions.rationale: κάμνω with the infinitive means to grow weary in doing something, and ἀντιβάλλω here means to set forth or relate.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: σχεδὸν καθ᾿ ἡμέραν τὴν ἀγαθήν σου ποιούμενος μνήμην
lexical_decisions.chosen: making favorable mention of you almost every day
lexical_decisions.rationale: ποιεῖσθαι μνήμην means to make mention or remembrance; ἀγαθήν marks that mention as favorable.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὧν κατὰ πόλιν ποιεῖσθαι μέλλω μέχρι Ῥώμης αὐτῆς
lexical_decisions.chosen: that I am about to deliver city by city, all the way to Rome itself
lexical_decisions.rationale: ποιεῖσθαι λόγους denotes giving or delivering discourses, while κατὰ πόλιν indicates successive activity in each city.

passages.text:
And I set out my purpose from the beginning, how I had exhausted myself in insoluble inquiries, and everything that I disclosed to you at the outset, so that I may not write the same things again. I said, “I am quite ready to travel with you—for, though I do not know how, this is what I gladly desire. But first I want to be fully assured about the truth, so that I may know whether the soul proves to be mortal or is immortal; whether, if it is eternal, it is to be judged for what it has done here; whether there is ever anything just or pleasing to God; whether the world came into being and why it came into being; whether it will not be dissolved and whether it will be dissolved; and whether it will be better or will not even exist.” And, to avoid speaking item by item, I said that I wanted to learn these things and those that follow from them.

In reply he said, “I will briefly give you knowledge of the things that exist, Clement; for the present, hear from that knowledge.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: I had exhausted myself in insoluble inquiries
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive form of κενόω is figurative here: the inquiries had left the speaker spent or emptied, while ἄπορος describes questions offering no way through.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦτο γὰρ οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως χαίρων θέλω
lexical_decisions.chosen: for, though I do not know how, this is what I gladly desire
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves the parenthetical uncertainty of οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως and the positive force of χαίρων θέλω; alternatively, the phrase may mean “for somehow—I do not know how—I gladly desire this.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: first I want to be fully assured about the truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: πληροφορέω denotes being brought to full assurance or certainty, not merely receiving information.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ εἰ ἀίδιος οὖσα περὶ ὧν ἔπραξεν ἐνταῦθα ἔχει κριθῆναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: whether, if it is eternal, it is to be judged for what it has done here
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main rendering takes ἀίδιος οὖσα conditionally because the preceding question leaves the soul’s immortality unsettled. The participle can alternatively state the circumstance or premise: “whether, being eternal, it is to be judged for what it has done here.” This is an interpretive ambiguity rather than source corruption.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: περὶ ὧν ἔπραξεν ἐνταῦθα ἔχει κριθῆναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: it is to be judged for what it has done here
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἔχει with the infinitive expresses what is appointed or bound to occur; the feminine subject remains the soul.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἴ τι ποτ᾿ ἔστιν δίκαιον ἢ ἀρέσκον θεῷ
lexical_decisions.chosen: whether there is ever anything just or pleasing to God
lexical_decisions.rationale: τι ποτε asks whether any such thing exists at all, while both adjectives remain coordinated.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ εἰ κρείττων ἔσται ἢ οὐδὲ ἔσται
lexical_decisions.chosen: and whether it will be better or will not even exist
lexical_decisions.rationale: οὐδέ supplies emphatic negation: the alternative to the world being better is that it will not even exist, not merely that it will no longer exist.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ τὸ κατ᾿ εἶδος λέγω
lexical_decisions.chosen: to avoid speaking item by item
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατ᾿ εἶδος can mean by individual form, category, or particular item; the context abbreviates a longer enumeration.

lexical_decisions.chosen: for the present, hear from that knowledge
lexical_decisions.rationale: τὰ νῦν is temporal, while αὐτῆς most naturally refers back to the promised knowledge; “hear the present points from it” is also possible.

passages.text:
God’s counsel has come to be hidden in many ways. First: bad initial instruction, evil upbringing, pernicious habit, bad company, and mistaken preconception. Because of these, error, then fearlessness, unbelief, sexual immorality, love of money, empty glory, and countless other such evils, like a mass of smoke occupying the world as a single house and clouding the vision of the men living inside, did not allow them, when they looked up, to discern from the design the God who made it or to recognize what pleases him.

Therefore, the lovers of truth who are inside must cry out from their breasts and summon help with truth-loving reasoning, so that someone who is outside the smoke-filled house may approach and open a door. Then the sunlight outside can be admitted into the house, and the smoke from the fire inside can be driven out.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ βουλὴ ἐν ἀδήλῳ γέγονεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: God’s counsel has come to be hidden
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐν ἀδήλῳ describes something placed in obscurity or uncertainty; “has become obscure” is a viable alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: bad initial instruction, evil upbringing
lexical_decisions.rationale: εἰσαγωγή is an introduction or initial course of instruction, while συντροφία can denote nurture or upbringing as well as companionship.

lexical_decisions.chosen: fearlessness
lexical_decisions.rationale: The term literally denotes absence of fear; in this catalogue it likely means culpable lack of fear, but the translation preserves the concise wording.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς ἕνα οἶκον οἰκοῦντα τὸν κόσμον
lexical_decisions.chosen: occupying the world as a single house
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle continues the smoke image and presents the world as the one house filled by the mass of evils.

lexical_decisions.chosen: from the design
lexical_decisions.rationale: διαγραφή may denote an outline, depiction, plan, or ordered design; “design” fits the inference from the visible world to its maker.

lexical_decisions.chosen: summon help with truth-loving reasoning
lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative φιλαλήθει λογισμῷ is taken instrumentally; it could also characterize the reasoning with which they cry out.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ μὲν ἐκτὸς τοῦ ἡλίου φῶς
lexical_decisions.chosen: the sunlight outside
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase contrasts the light outside the house with the smoke inside; a more formal rendering is “the external light of the sun.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁ δὲ ἐντὸς τοῦ πυρὸς ὢν ἐκβληθῆναι καπνός
lexical_decisions.chosen: the smoke from the fire inside can be driven out
lexical_decisions.rationale: The word order permits either “the smoke from the fire inside” or “the smoke inside, arising from the fire”; the former keeps the spatial contrast clear.

passages.text:
By “the helper,” then, I mean the man who is the true prophet. He alone can illuminate human souls, so that we may be able to see with our own eyes the road of eternal salvation. Otherwise this is impossible, as you yourself know, having said a little earlier that every thesis can be refuted and established, and that the same thesis comes to be regarded as true and false according to the ability of the person defending it. Consequently, theses no longer appear as what they are but, depending on their defenders, acquire the appearance of being or not being true or false.

For this reason, the whole matter of piety needed a true prophet, so that he might tell us what exists as it is and how one must believe about everything. One must therefore first test the prophet by the full prophetic examination and recognize him as true. After that, one must believe him in everything and no longer scrutinize each individual thing said by him, but receive those things as certain. They are apparently received by faith, but in fact by secure judgment; for by a single proof from the outset and by a precise examination from every side, all things have been rightly grasped by sound reasoning. Therefore, above all else, one must seek the true prophet, because without him it is impossible for anything certain to be available to human beings.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν μὲν οὖν βοηθὸν ἄνδρα τὸν ἀληθῆ προφήτην λέγω
lexical_decisions.chosen: By “the helper,” then, I mean the man who is the true prophet
lexical_decisions.rationale: The two accusative expressions stand in apposition: the assisting man is identified as the true prophet.

lexical_decisions.chosen: so that we may be able to see with our own eyes
lexical_decisions.rationale: αὐτοῖς is intensive here, emphasizing direct sight rather than sight mediated by another person.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς οἶσθα καὶ σύ, μικρῷ τάχιον εἰπὼν
lexical_decisions.chosen: as you yourself know, having said a little earlier
lexical_decisions.rationale: The nominative participle εἰπών is taken with the explicit local subject σύ, making the addressee the person who stated the point a little earlier.

lexical_decisions.chosen: every thesis can be refuted and established
lexical_decisions.rationale: In argumentative usage, ἀνασκευάζω means dismantle or refute a case, while κατασκευάζω means construct or establish it.

lexical_decisions.chosen: according to the ability of the person defending it
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐκδικέω here concerns advocacy or defense of a position, not punishment or vengeance.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: προφήτου ἀληθοῦς ὅλον τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας ἐδεήθη πρᾶγμα
lexical_decisions.chosen: the whole matter of piety needed a true prophet
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive προφήτου depends on the verb of need, and τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας πρᾶγμα denotes the entire undertaking or matter of piety.

lexical_decisions.chosen: by the full prophetic examination
lexical_decisions.rationale: The articular singular ἐξετάσει presents the prophetic examination as a whole, while πάσῃ gives it comprehensive force rather than dividing it into separate tests.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δοκούσῃ μὲν πίστει, ληφθέντα δὲ ἀσφαλεῖ κρίσει
lexical_decisions.chosen: They are apparently received by faith, but in fact by secure judgment
lexical_decisions.rationale: The contrast distinguishes the appearance of unexamined faith from the prior reliable judgment by which the prophet was authenticated.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀποδείξει γὰρ μιᾷ τῇ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς καὶ ἀκριβεῖ ἐξετάσει τῇ πανταχόθεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: for by a single proof from the outset and by a precise examination from every side
lexical_decisions.rationale: The two datives are read as coordinated: the single proof is characterized as being from the outset, and the precise examination as being from every side. Alternatively, καί may be explanatory, making the examination appositional to the proof, but the coordinated reading most directly preserves the construction.

lexical_decisions.chosen: all things have been rightly grasped by sound reasoning
lexical_decisions.rationale: τὰ ὅλα denotes the totality of the matters in question, while ὀρθῷ λογισμῷ identifies the sound reasoning by which they have been grasped.

lexical_decisions.chosen: anything certain to be available to human beings
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρόσειμι means to be present or available; “for human beings to possess any certainty” conveys the same contextual force.

passages.text:
And likewise he set my mind at rest by explaining to me who he is and how he is found, and by actually enabling me to find him. Through the discourse about the prophet he showed the truth to my ears more plainly than things seen before the eyes, so that I was astonished and wondered how, when the things sought by everyone lie before them, no one perceives them.

However, after the discourse about the prophet had been written at his command, he arranged for the volume to be sent to you from Caesarea Stratonis, saying that he had a command from you each year to write down and send you the discourses and deeds. Nevertheless, on that single first day, while only just beginning to speak about the prophet of truth, he fully assured me about everything. Then he spoke as follows:

“From now on, observe the debates that I conduct against the opponents. Even if I come off worse, I am not afraid that you will doubt the truth handed down to you, since you know that it was I who appeared to be defeated, not the thesis handed down to us through the prophet. Still, I hope not to come off worse even in the testing debate, at least in the judgment of those who have understanding—I mean lovers of truth. They can recognize which arguments are persuasive, artfully constructed, and entertaining, and which are plain and simple, relying only on the truth conveyed through them.”

source_issues.source_quote: ὁμῶς
source_issues.issue: The supplied, image-checked print has ὁμῶς, which can support “likewise,” whereas the much more usual concessive adverb ὅμως would mean “nevertheless.” The translation preserves the printed form; the interpretation remains provisional rather than silently adopting the conjecture.

source_issues.source_quote: πλὴν γράψας τὸν περὶ προφήτου λόγον, αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος, ἀπὸ τῆς Καισαρείας τῆς Στράτωνος διαπεμφθῆναί σοι ἐποίησεν τὸν τόμον
source_issues.issue: The nominative active participle γράψας would ordinarily share the subject of ἐποίησεν, but the genitive absolute αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος and the surrounding first-person narrative make the identities of the writer, commander, and person arranging dispatch uncertain. The translation uses an English passive for the writing event to avoid assigning an unsupported identity; a same-subject rendering, “after writing the discourse … he arranged,” is grammatically possible but leaves the command-giver’s referent unresolved.

lexical_decisions.chosen: likewise he set my mind at rest
lexical_decisions.rationale: The translation follows the supplied ὁμῶς as an adverb of similarity and takes ἀναπαύω figuratively as relieving uncertainty.

lexical_decisions.chosen: by actually enabling me to find him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Literally, the speaker was provided with the prophet as someone truly findable; the English expresses the resulting ability without adding an identity.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through the discourse about the prophet
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive is read objectively because the preceding explanation concerns who the prophet is. “Through the prophet’s discourse” remains grammatically possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: when the things sought by everyone lie before them
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive absolute presents the sought realities as already lying openly before people.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the volume
lexical_decisions.rationale: τόμος here denotes a written book-roll or volume containing the discourse.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰς καθ’ ἕκαστον ἐνιαυτὸν ὁμιλίας τε καὶ πράξεις γράφοντα διαπέμπειν σοι
lexical_decisions.chosen: each year to write down and send you the discourses and deeds
lexical_decisions.rationale: καθ’ ἕκαστον ἐνιαυτόν is taken adverbially with the recurring writing and dispatch; it could instead characterize the contents as “the discourses and deeds of each year.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: From now on, observe
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐνοράω calls for attentive observation, while τοῦ λοιποῦ marks the time from this point onward.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: περὶ τῆς παραδοθείσης σοι ἀληθείας διακριθήσῃ
lexical_decisions.chosen: you will doubt the truth handed down to you
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this context διακρίνω denotes inward wavering or doubt, though “be divided in judgment about” is more formally possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: since you know that it was I who appeared to be defeated
lexical_decisions.rationale: εἰδώς is attached to the explicitly addressed σύ because the point is that the hearer can distinguish the debater’s apparent defeat from that of the thesis. Attachment to the speaker, “since I know,” is also syntactically possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in the testing debate
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐξεταστικός characterizes the λόγος as examining, testing, or critically probing the positions under debate; it does not describe an argument that is itself merely under examination.

lexical_decisions.chosen: persuasive, artfully constructed, and entertaining
lexical_decisions.rationale: The three adjectives describe rhetorical appeal, technical craftsmanship, and pleasurable effect, in contrast with plain arguments relying on truth alone.
